passage:
Lalremsiami had drafted the message to Shalini four times and deleted it four times. Three weeks as manager in a Bengaluru logistics office, and the shift rota had collapsed twice. Asking felt like admitting failure.

On Friday Lalremsiami wrote down two things: the problem (two people always swap shifts at the last minute, leaving gaps) and three options: fixed swap rules, a shared sign-up sheet, or a buffer person. Then the message went: "Shalini, could I have twenty minutes? I have a scheduling problem and three ideas, and I'd like your view."

Shalini replied within minutes. "Good. Come Monday. I made the same mess in my first year."

The relief was physical. On Monday Shalini pointed out that the sign-up sheet needed a deadline rule. Lalremsiami left with a plan and a monthly slot on Shalini's calendar.

qa.q: How many options did Lalremsiami bring to Shalini?
qa.a: Lalremsiami brought three options: fixed swap rules, a shared sign-up sheet or a buffer person.

qa.q: Why did Lalremsiami delete the message four times?
qa.a: Asking felt like admitting failure, so Lalremsiami hesitated.

qa.q: What made Lalremsiami's request for help effective?
qa.a: Lalremsiami named the problem, brought three options and asked for twenty minutes to hear Shalini's view.

qa.q: How did Shalini see the request?
qa.a: Shalini welcomed it, saying 'Good. Come Monday,' and shared having made the same mess in the first year.

grounding: A new manager feels lost and hesitates to ask a boss for help, then brings a specific problem and options and asks for coaching early.

passage:
Tuesday night.

Third week as a manager and I have no idea what I'm doing. Two people on my team aren't talking to each other. The budget spreadsheet makes no sense. I've been staying till nine pretending I'm fine.

Nitin sir, my own boss, keeps saying "Come to me any time, young man." And I keep not going, because I'm scared he'll think promoting me was a mistake.

Today I noticed something. When I avoid him, the problems just sit there getting bigger.

So I wrote down the two problems properly. For the team conflict: option A, sit them down together; option B, talk to each separately first. For the budget: I'll ask Rukhsana from finance for thirty minutes, or Nitin sir could explain the categories.

Tomorrow at ten I'm going to his office with this page. Not "I'm lost." Just "Here's the problem, here's what I'm thinking, what would you do?"

I'm Raghav, and asking isn't failing. I hope.

qa.q: How many problems did Raghav write down for Nitin sir?
What was Raghav afraid of when avoiding Nitin sir?
qa.a: Raghav was scared that Nitin sir would think promoting him was a mistake.

qa.q: Why is Raghav's page a good way to ask for help?
qa.a: It brings specific problems with options instead of just worry, which makes coaching quick and shows he is thinking.

qa.q: How might Nitin sir feel when Raghav comes in with the page?
qa.a: Nitin sir will probably feel pleased and reassured, since he has been inviting Raghav to come to him.

grounding: A diary entry shows a new manager who feels lost and hesitates to ask his boss for help, then decides to bring specific problems and options for coaching.

passage:
Nirmala: Lavanya ma'am, do you have 20 mins this week? I need some coaching
Lavanya: of course. what's up?
Nirmala: I've been putting this off because I didn't want you to think I can't handle the team 😅
Lavanya: asking early is exactly what good managers do. go on
Nirmala: two things. first, Pritam keeps missing handover notes and the night shift suffers
Nirmala: I could a) have a direct talk with a written plan, or b) pair him with Sister Grace for a week
Nirmala: second, the leave roster for Christmas. everyone wants the same days
Nirmala: I was thinking a lottery, or rotating from last year. not sure which is fairer
Lavanya: honestly these are great options. you've done the hard thinking already
Lavanya: Thursday 3pm? bring the roster
Nirmala: thank you ma'am 🙏 I feel lighter already
Lavanya: next time don't wait three weeks to ask, okay? 🙂

qa.q: Which two options did Nirmala suggest for Pritam's missed handover notes?
qa.a: A direct talk with a written plan, or pairing him with Sister Grace for a week.

qa.q: What was Nirmala worried about before asking?
qa.a: Nirmala was worried and a bit embarrassed that Lavanya would think the team was too much to handle.

qa.q: Why did Lavanya respond so positively?
qa.a: Because Nirmala asked early and brought specific problems with options, which makes coaching easy and shows good judgment.

qa.q: How does Lavanya see asking for help?
qa.a: Lavanya sees it as a strength and wishes Nirmala hadn't waited three weeks.

grounding: A chat shows a new manager who hesitated to ask the boss for help, then asks for coaching with specific problems and options and is welcomed.
